//   semantics/functions.k      MPY-FUNCTIONS    def / call / return (frame stack)
//   semantics/builtins.k       MPY-BUILTINS     builtins as calls: len/sum/abs/min/max/ord/chr/str
//   semantics/call.k           MPY-CALL         ALL Call routing + argument evaluation
//   semantics/sort.k           MPY-SORT         trusted sorted(): opaque sortVS + concrete insertion sort
//   semantics/assert.k         MPY-ASSERT       Assert oracle (smoke programs only)
//   semantics/dict.k           MPY-DICT         order-preserving dictV(KS,VS) + .keys() + list()

requires "semantics/syntax.k"
requires "semantics/core.k"
requires "semantics/iter.k"
requires "semantics/range.k"
requires "semantics/operators.k"
requires "semantics/int.k"
requires "semantics/bool.k"
requires "semantics/float.k"
requires "semantics/str.k"
requires "semantics/set.k"
requires "semantics/list.k"
requires "semantics/tuple.k"
requires "semantics/subscript.k"
requires "semantics/comprehension.k"
requires "semantics/methods.k"
requires "semantics/controls.k"
requires "semantics/functions.k"
requires "semantics/builtins.k"
requires "semantics/call.k"
requires "semantics/sort.k"
requires "semantics/assert.k"
requires "semantics/dict.k"
requires "semantics/concrete.k"

module MPY
  imports MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-ITER
  imports MPY-RANGE
  imports MPY-OPERATORS
  imports MPY-INT
  imports MPY-BOOL
  imports MPY-FLOAT
  imports MPY-STR
  imports MPY-SET
  imports MPY-LIST
  imports MPY-TUPLE
  imports MPY-SUBSCRIPT
  imports MPY-COMPREHENSION
  imports MPY-METHODS
  imports MPY-CONTROLS
  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS
  imports MPY-BUILTINS
  imports MPY-CALL
  imports MPY-SORT
  imports MPY-ASSERT
  imports MPY-DICT
endmodule

// The krun (llvm) main module: MPY plus the concrete-only legs (keyed sort's
// real key calls, deep list equality). Verification builds import MPY and
// never see MPY-CONCRETE. The llvm kompile MUST use --main-module MPY-KRUN —
// with plain MPY the concrete legs are silently absent (this was live for a
// while: sorted-key stuck and comprehension asserted wrong under krun).
module MPY-KRUN
  imports MPY
  imports MPY-CONCRETE
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/syntax.k — MPY-SYNTAX

module MPY-SYNTAX
  imports INT-SYNTAX
  imports FLOAT-SYNTAX
  imports BOOL-SYNTAX
  imports STRING-SYNTAX

  syntax Expr ::= "Int"      "(" Int ")"
                | "Float"    "(" Float ")"
                | "Bool"     "(" Bool ")"
                | "Name"     "(" String ")"
                | "Str"      "(" String ")"
                | "UnaryOp"  "(" String "," Expr ")" [strict(2)]
                | "BinOp"    "(" String "," Expr "," Expr ")" [seqstrict(2, 3)]
                | "BoolOp"    "(" String "," Exprs ")"
                | "ListExpr"  "(" Exprs ")"
                | "DictExpr"  "(" Entries ")"
                | "ListComp"  "(" Expr "," CompFors ")" [macro]
                | "GenExp"    "(" Expr "," CompFors ")" [macro]
                | "TupleExpr" "(" Exprs ")"
                | "Subscript" "(" Expr "," Index ")"
                | "IfExp"     "(" Expr "," Expr "," Expr ")" [strict(1)]
                | "Lambda"    "(" Params "," Expr ")"
                | "KwArg"     "(" String "," Expr ")"
                | "Lambda"    "(" Params "," CellVars "," FreeVars "," Expr ")"
                | "NoneVal"
                | "Call"      "(" Expr "," Exprs ")"
                | "Attribute" "(" Expr "," String ")" [strict(1)]
                | "Compare"   "(" Expr "," CmpOp ")"

  syntax CmpOp    ::= "CmpOp" "(" String "," Expr ")"
  syntax Entry    ::= "Entry" "(" Expr "," Expr ")"
  syntax Entries  ::= List{Entry, ","}
  syntax CompFor  ::= "CompFor" "(" Expr "," Expr "," Exprs ")"
  syntax CompFors ::= List{CompFor, ""}
  syntax Exprs    ::= List{Expr, ","}
  syntax Index    ::= Expr | "Slice" "(" Bound "," Bound "," Bound ")"
  syntax Bound    ::= Expr | "NoBound"

  syntax Stmt ::= "Assign"    "(" Expr "," Expr ")" [strict(2)]
                | "Import"    "(" String ")"
                | "ImportFrom" "(" String "," ParamNames ")"
                | "AugAssign" "(" Expr "," String "," Expr ")" [strict(3)]
                | "For"       "(" Expr "," Expr "," Stmts ")" [strict(2)]
                | "While"     "(" Expr "," Stmts ")"
                | "Break"
                | "Continue"
                | "If"        "(" Expr "," Stmts "," Stmts ")" [strict(1)]
                | "Return"    "(" Expr ")" [strict]
                | "Assert"    "(" Expr ")" [strict]
                | "Expr"      "(" Expr ")" [strict]
                | "FuncDef"   "(" String "," Params "," Stmts ")"
                | "FuncDef"   "(" String "," Params "," CellVars "," FreeVars "," Stmts ")"

  syntax Stmts      ::= List{Stmt, ""}
  syntax Params     ::= "Params" "(" ParamNames ")"
  syntax CellVars   ::= "CellVars" "(" ParamNames ")"
  syntax FreeVars   ::= "FreeVars" "(" ParamNames ")"
  syntax ParamNames ::= List{String, ","}
  syntax Module     ::= "Module" "(" Stmts ")"
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/core.k — MPY-CORE

module MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-SYNTAX
  imports INT
  imports BOOL
  imports STRING
  imports MAP
  imports LIST
  imports K-EQUAL

  // ==== values, the algebraic lists, and the scope heap =====================
  syntax IntSeq ::= ".IntSeq" | iCons(Int, IntSeq)
  syntax ValSeq ::= ".ValSeq" | vCons(Val, ValSeq)
  syntax Str    ::= str(IntSeq)

  // the iterable values, grouped under one sort (typing only — dispatch is <k>-cell)
  syntax Iterable ::= list(ValSeq)
                    | tuple(ValSeq)
                    | Str
                    | rangeObj(Int, Int, Int)
                    | zipObj(ValSeq, ValSeq)
                    | zipObjS(IntSeq, IntSeq)

  syntax Val      ::= Int
                    | Bool
                    | "noneV"
                    | Iterable
                    | ref(Int)          // a heap object: <heap> holds its list(VS)
                    | cellRef(Int)      // a closure cell: <heap> holds cellV(V)
                    | closureVal(ParamNames, Stmts, Int)
                    | typeV(String)     // a type object (int/str), resolved from the builtins frame
                    | builtinV(String)  // a builtin function, resolved like any name (LEGB fallthrough)
                    | boundMethodV(Val, String)   // a cooled Attribute: obj.method

  syntax Parent   ::= "root" | parent(Int)
  syntax Scope    ::= scope(Map, Parent)
  syntax KResult  ::= Val
  syntax Expr     ::= Val   // cooling puts results back into expression holes
  syntax Vals     ::= List{Val, ","}
  syntax Exc      ::= "NoExc" | "AssertionError"
  syntax RetState ::= "noRet" | retV(Val)

  // ==== configuration =======================================================
  // The builtins namespace is a real scope at reserved location -1 (the bottom of every
  // chain; scopeLoc only allocates >=1, so -1 never collides). The module scope (loc 0)
  // has it as parent, so an unbound name resolves there last — exactly LEGB. `int`/`str`
  // resolve to their type objects; any local/global binding shadows them via normal lookup.
  configuration
    <k>       #loadAll($PGM:Module) </k>
    <env>     0 </env>
    <scopes>   0     |-> scope(.Map, parent(-1))
              -1    |-> builtinsScope </scopes>
    <scopeLoc> 1 </scopeLoc>
    <heap>    .Map </heap>
    <heapLoc> 0 </heapLoc>
    <stack>   .List </stack>
    <ret>     noRet </ret>
    <exc>     NoExc </exc>
    <exit-code exit=""> 0 </exit-code>

  // ==== heap allocation (constructed lists become objects) ==================
  // Cons-form emission with a freshness guard (the heap-list-probe discipline:
  // an update-form H[N <- _] never re-normalizes symbolically). heapLoc is
  // monotonic — it does NOT wind back at #pop: returned lists escape by ref.
  // A bare list(VS) Val stays legal (read-only inputs in claims flow unboxed);
  // only CONSTRUCTORS in program syntax allocate.
  syntax Bool ::= isRefV(Val) [function, total]
  rule isRefV(ref(_:Int)) => true
  rule isRefV(_:Val)      => false [owise]

  // closure cells (Python-faithful capture): the heap holds cellV(V); a
  // cellRef surfacing as the k-redex reads through (lookup is the only use —
  // cellRefs never escape to user-visible values)
  syntax HeapVal ::= cellV(Val)
  syntax Bool ::= isCellRef(Val) [function, total]
  rule isCellRef(cellRef(_:Int)) => true
  rule isCellRef(_:Val)          => false [owise]
  // k-top deref for cell-bound reads surfacing INSIDE the annotated frame
  // (AugAssign's in-place read and friends). The "$cells" guard keeps this
  // DECIDABLY inapplicable in plain frames — an unguarded rule lets the
  // prover narrow abstract k-top values into cellRef junk (probed on
  // 26-remove-duplicates). Cross-frame reads (a comprehension closure
  // reading the enclosing function's cellvar) deref inside #look instead.
  rule <k> cellRef(H:Int) => V ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(V:Val) ... </heap>
       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
       [priority(40)]

  // write through a cell (Assign / #bindP / #bindTgt dispatch here on
  // cell-bound names)
  // a keyword argument cools to a TAGGED value (consumed by kw-aware builtins)
  syntax Val ::= kwV(String, Val)
  syntax KItem ::= #kwTag(String)
  rule <k> KwArg(N:String, E:Expr) => E ~> #kwTag(N) ... </k>
  rule <k> V:Val ~> #kwTag(N:String) => kwV(N, V) ... </k>
       requires notBool isKwV(V)
  syntax Bool ::= isKwV(Val) [function, total]
  rule isKwV(kwV(_:String, _:Val)) => true
  rule isKwV(_:Val)                => false [owise]

  // the frame marker carries the CONCRETE cellvar list, so cell-write dispatch
  // decides by pnMember even over an abstract frame rest (no prover branching)
  syntax Val ::= cellsMark(ParamNames)
  syntax ParamNames ::= cellsOf(Val) [function]
  rule cellsOf(cellsMark(CVS:ParamNames)) => CVS
  syntax Bool ::= pnMember(String, ParamNames) [function, total]
  rule pnMember(_:String, .ParamNames) => false
  rule pnMember(X:String, (P:String, R:ParamNames)) => X ==String P orBool pnMember(X, R)

  syntax KItem ::= #cellW(Val, Val)
  rule <k> #cellW(cellRef(H:Int), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(_:Val => V) ... </heap>

  syntax KItem ::= #alloc(Val)
  rule <k> #alloc(V:Val) => ref(N) ... </k>
       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> V) H </heap>
       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
       requires notBool N in_keys(H)

  // ==== module load + statement sequencing ==================================
  syntax KItem ::= #loadAll(Module)
  rule <k> #loadAll(Module(SS:Stmts)) => SS ... </k>
  rule <k> (S:Stmt SS:Stmts):Stmts => S ~> SS ... </k>
  rule <k> .Stmts => .K ... </k>

  // ==== Name lookup (walk the scope chain; builtins live in the -1 scope) ====
  syntax KItem ::= #look(String, Int)
  rule <k> Name(X:String) => #look(X, L) ... </k> <env> L:Int </env>
  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => {M[X]}:>Val ... </k>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires X in_keys(M)
  // a SYNTACTICALLY cell-bound name reads through the heap cell AT THE
  // LOOKUP (higher priority beats the plain return above on concrete cell
  // bindings; abstract claim values take the plain rule unchanged) — this
  // covers cross-frame cell reads (a comprehension closure reading the
  // enclosing function's cellvar) without a narrowing-prone k-top redex
  // guarded on the FOUND frame's DECLARED cellvars (pnMember over the
  // cellsMark): decidable for every concrete frame pin — plain frames and
  // non-cell names prune outright, so an abstract looked-up value never
  // drags a narrowing cellV heap match along (probed on 5-intersperse and
  // Q4's abstract `numbers` in the annotated frame)
  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => V ... </k>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(V:Val) ... </heap>
       requires X in_keys(M) andBool "$cells" in_keys(M)
        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
        andBool {M[X]}:>Val ==K cellRef(H)
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => #look(X, P) ... </k>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, parent(P:Int)) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))

  // the ONE predefined builtins scope (the -1 frame; claims write `-1 |-> builtinsScope`)
  syntax Scope ::= "builtinsScope" [function, total]
  rule builtinsScope
    => scope(.Map [ "len"    <- builtinV("len")    ]
                  [ "set"    <- builtinV("set")    ]
                  [ "sum"    <- builtinV("sum")    ]
                  [ "abs"    <- builtinV("abs")    ]
                  [ "min"    <- builtinV("min")    ]
                  [ "max"    <- builtinV("max")    ]
                  [ "ord"    <- builtinV("ord")    ]
                  [ "chr"    <- builtinV("chr")    ]
                  [ "range"  <- builtinV("range")  ]
                  [ "all"    <- builtinV("all")    ]
                  [ "any"    <- builtinV("any")    ]
                  [ "zip"    <- builtinV("zip")    ]
                  [ "isinstance" <- builtinV("isinstance") ]
                  [ "sorted" <- builtinV("sorted") ]
                  [ "list"   <- builtinV("list")   ]
                  [ "round"  <- builtinV("round")  ]
                  [ "bin"    <- builtinV("bin")    ]
                  [ "enumerate" <- builtinV("enumerate") ]
                  [ "map"    <- builtinV("map")    ]
                  [ "eval"   <- builtinV("eval")   ]
                  [ "int"    <- typeV("int")       ]
                  [ "str"    <- typeV("str")       ]
                  [ "float"  <- typeV("float")     ], root)

  // ==== argument/element evaluation: ONE left-to-right loop, tagged by destination ==
  // (list/tuple literals and calls all use it; modules extend ApplyK with their tags)
  syntax ApplyK ::= toCall(Val)
  syntax KItem  ::= #evalArgs(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
                  | #evalArgCont(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
                  | #applyK(ApplyK, Vals)
  rule <k> #evalArgs((A:Expr, REST:Exprs), ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => A ~> #evalArgCont(REST, ACC, K) ... </k>
  rule <k> V:Val ~> #evalArgCont(REST:Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #evalArgs(REST, appendVal(ACC, V), K) ... </k>
  rule <k> #evalArgs(.Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #applyK(K, ACC) ... </k>

  // ==== Int / Bool / None literals ==========================================
  rule <k> Int(I:Int)   => I ... </k>
  rule <k> Bool(B:Bool) => B ... </k>
  rule <k> NoneVal      => noneV ... </k>

  // ==== truthy (If, Assert, BoolOp, IfExp, not, While) ======================
  syntax Bool ::= truthy(Val) [function]
  rule truthy(B:Bool)          => B
  rule truthy(noneV)           => false
  rule truthy(I:Int)           => I =/=Int 0
  rule truthy(str(S:IntSeq))   => notBool (S ==K .IntSeq)
  rule truthy(list(V:ValSeq))  => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
  rule truthy(tuple(V:ValSeq)) => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)

  // ==== extensible operator dispatch (cases added by the construct modules) ==
  syntax Val  ::= applyUn(String, Val) [function]
  syntax Val  ::= applyBin(String, Val, Val) [function]
  syntax Bool ::= applyCmp(String, Val, Val) [function]

  // ==== shared list helpers =================================================
  syntax Vals ::= appendVal(Vals, Val) [function, total]
  rule appendVal(.Vals, V:Val)              => V , .Vals
  rule appendVal((V0:Val, VS:Vals), V:Val)  => V0 , appendVal(VS, V)

  syntax ValSeq ::= vals2valSeq(Vals) [function, total]
  rule vals2valSeq(.Vals)            => .ValSeq
  rule vals2valSeq((V:Val, VS:Vals)) => vCons(V, vals2valSeq(VS))

  // ==== shared sequence length (len / summaries across many modules) ========
  // (positional access valSeqAt/intSeqAt + normIdx live in subscript.k)
  syntax Int ::= vsLen(ValSeq) [function, total]
  rule vsLen(.ValSeq)                => 0
  rule vsLen(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq)) => 1 +Int vsLen(S)

  syntax Int ::= isLen(IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule isLen(.IntSeq)                => 0
  rule isLen(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq)) => 1 +Int isLen(S)

  // in-bounds positional write (list subscript-assign); OOB leaves the seq unchanged
  // (valid programs write in-bounds — mirrors valSeqAt's total-but-underspecified stance)
  syntax ValSeq ::= setVSAt(ValSeq, Int, Val) [function, total]
  rule setVSAt(.ValSeq, _:Int, _:Val)               => .ValSeq
  rule setVSAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), 0, V:Val)    => vCons(V, S)
  rule setVSAt(vCons(W:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int, V:Val) => vCons(W, setVSAt(S, I -Int 1, V))
       requires I >Int 0
  rule setVSAt(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, _:Val)             => VS
       requires I <Int 0
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/float.k — MPY-FLOAT
//
// Minimal, TRUSTED float support. K/Haskell (kprove) has no usable symbolic IEEE-754 theory and
// no Int2Float hook, so a float value stays an OPAQUE proof-domain primitive: `intFloatDiv(I, F)`
// (the Python true division I / F) is `[no-evaluators]` for kprove — it never reduces on symbolic
// input, and the proof verifies only the STRUCTURE (the result is the exact term the program
// builds). The `[concrete]` rule evaluates it for krun (llvm HAS the Int2Float / /Float hooks), so
// smoke tests run the real float value.
//
// Only the pieces needed so far: Float as a Val, the float literal, and Int / float true division
// (the `a * h / 2.0` idiom). More float ops (float +/-/*, comparison) are added as float problems
// need them — kept minimal + sound.

module MPY-FLOAT
  imports MPY-OPERATORS
  imports MPY-BUILTINS
  imports FLOAT

  // Float is a value; the float literal evaluates to the K Float.
  syntax Val ::= Float
  rule <k> Float(F:Float) => F ... </k>

  // Int / float true division. OPAQUE for kprove (no-evaluators); concrete for krun.
  syntax Float ::= intFloatDiv(Int, Float) [function, total, symbol(intFloatDiv), no-evaluators]
  rule intFloatDiv(I:Int, F:Float) => Int2Float(I,…775 tokens truncated…from math import floor, ceil`)
  rule applyBuiltin("floor", V:Val, .Vals) => floorFI(V)
  rule applyBuiltin("ceil",  V:Val, .Vals) => ceilF(V)

  // math.pow(x, y) — a two-arg interception onto powF (ints promote)
  syntax KItem ::= #mathPow1(Expr) | #mathPow2(Val)
  rule <k> Call(Attribute(Name("math"), "pow"), (E1:Expr, E2:Expr, .Exprs)) => E1 ~> #mathPow1(E2) ... </k> [priority(40)]
  rule <k> V1:Val ~> #mathPow1(E2:Expr) => E2 ~> #mathPow2(V1) ... </k>
  rule <k> V2:Val ~> #mathPow2(V1:Val) => powF(toF(V1), toF(V2)) ... </k>
  syntax Float ::= toF(Val) [function, total, symbol(toF)]
  rule toF(F:Float) => F        [concrete]
  rule toF(I:Int)   => intToF(I) [concrete]

  // ceilF: math.ceil as an Int. TOTAL (K trusts it; a symbolic list element stays opaque for
  // kprove — structural). [concrete] so the Int2Float/ceilFloat hooks only run for krun (llvm).
  // Matches Python incl. negatives: ceil(-2.4) = -2 = Float2Int(ceilFloat(-2.4)).
  syntax Int ::= ceilF(Val) [function, total, symbol(ceilF)]
  rule ceilF(I:Int)   => I                       [concrete]
  rule ceilF(F:Float) => Float2Int(ceilFloat(F)) [concrete]

  // unary minus on a float (e.g. the literal -2.4 = UnaryOp("-", Float(2.4))). Concrete for krun;
  // proofs use symbolic elements, never a float literal.
  rule applyUn("-", F:Float) => 0.0 -Float F

  // ---- float - / / / + (OPAQUE for kprove [no-evaluators], concrete for krun) — for float-list
  // element maps (x - lo) / (hi - lo). Mirror intFloatDiv: additive, sort-disjoint from the Int rules.
  syntax Float ::= subF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(subF), no-evaluators]
  rule subF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 -Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("-", F1:Float, F2:Float) => subF(F1, F2)

  syntax Float ::= divF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(divF), no-evaluators]
  rule divF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 /Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("/", F1:Float, F2:Float) => divF(F1, F2)

  syntax Float ::= addF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(addF), no-evaluators]
  rule addF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 +Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("+", F1:Float, F2:Float) => addF(F1, F2)

  syntax Float ::= mulF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(mulF), no-evaluators]
  rule mulF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 *Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("*", F1:Float, F2:Float) => mulF(F1, F2)

  syntax Float ::= powF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(powF), no-evaluators]
  rule powF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 ^Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("**", F1:Float, F2:Float) => powF(F1, F2)

  // ---- the remaining comparisons (gtF promoted from find_zero — its summaries
  //      case-split on the atom; >= / <= derive from the two opaque compares) ----
  syntax Bool ::= gtF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(gtF), no-evaluators]
  rule gtF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 >Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyCmp(">",  F1:Float, F2:Float) => gtF(F1, F2)
  rule applyCmp(">=", F1:Float, F2:Float) => notBool floatLt(F1, F2)
  rule applyCmp("<=", F1:Float, F2:Float) => notBool gtF(F1, F2)

  // ---- mixed Int/Float operators promote the Int side (n ** 0.5 etc.) ----
  rule applyBin("**", I:Int, F:Float) => powF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("**", F:Float, I:Int) => powF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyBin("-",  I:Int, F:Float) => subF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("-",  F:Float, I:Int) => subF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyBin("+",  I:Int, F:Float) => addF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("+",  F:Float, I:Int) => addF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyBin("*",  I:Int, F:Float) => mulF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("*",  F:Float, I:Int) => mulF(F, intToF(I))

  // ---- mixed Int == Float (shared eqF; opaque symbolic / concrete twin) ----
  syntax Bool ::= eqF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(eqF), no-evaluators]
  rule eqF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 ==Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyCmp("==", I:Int, F:Float) => eqF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp("==", F:Float, I:Int) => eqF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyCmp("!=", I:Int, F:Float) => notBool eqF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp("!=", F:Float, I:Int) => notBool eqF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyCmp("<",  I:Int, F:Float) => floatLt(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp("<",  F:Float, I:Int) => floatLt(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyCmp(">",  I:Int, F:Float) => gtF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp(">",  F:Float, I:Int) => gtF(F, intToF(I))

  // ---- x == None (promoted from 137; `is` cases live in operators.k) ----
  rule applyCmp("==", V:Val, noneV) => V ==K noneV
  rule applyCmp("!=", V:Val, noneV) => notBool (V ==K noneV)

  // ---- float(str): decimal parse (promoted from 137's defined chain) ----
  // digits '.' digits, optional leading '-'; concrete evaluation only (the
  // symbolic side stays an opaque decStrToF term a proof case-splits on).
  syntax Float ::= decStrToF(IntSeq) [function, total, symbol(decStrToF), no-evaluators]
  rule decStrToF(iCons(45, CS:IntSeq)) => 0.0 -Float decStrToF(CS) [concrete]
  rule decStrToF(CS:IntSeq)
    => intToF(intPart(CS)) +Float (intToF(fracPart(CS)) /Float intToF(fracScale(CS)))
       requires isLen(CS) >Int 0 andBool headIS(CS) =/=Int 45 [concrete]
  syntax Int ::= headIS(IntSeq) [function]
  rule headIS(iCons(C:Int, _:IntSeq)) => C
  syntax Int ::= intPart(IntSeq) [function, total] | intPartAcc(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
  rule intPart(CS:IntSeq) => intPartAcc(CS, 0)
  rule intPartAcc(.IntSeq, A:Int) => A
  rule intPartAcc(iCons(46, _:IntSeq), A:Int) => A
  rule intPartAcc(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), A:Int) => intPartAcc(R, A *Int 10 +Int (C -Int 48))
       requires C =/=Int 46
  syntax Int ::= fracPart(IntSeq) [function, total] | fracAcc(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
  rule fracPart(.IntSeq) => 0
  rule fracPart(iCons(46, R:IntSeq)) => fracAcc(R, 0)
  rule fracPart(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => fracPart(R) requires C =/=Int 46
  rule fracAcc(.IntSeq, A:Int) => A
  rule fracAcc(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), A:Int) => fracAcc(R, A *Int 10 +Int (C -Int 48))
  syntax Int ::= fracScale(IntSeq) [function, total] | fscAcc(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
  rule fracScale(.IntSeq) => 1
  rule fracScale(iCons(46, R:IntSeq)) => fscAcc(R, 1)
  rule fracScale(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => fracScale(R) requires C =/=Int 46
  rule fscAcc(.IntSeq, A:Int) => A
  rule fscAcc(iCons(_:Int, R:IntSeq), A:Int) => fscAcc(R, A *Int 10)
  rule applyBuiltin("float", str(CS:IntSeq), .Vals) => decStrToF(CS)
  rule applyBuiltin("float", I:Int, .Vals)          => intToF(I)
  rule applyBuiltin("float", F:Float, .Vals)        => F

  // ---- float / int division (promoted from mean_absolute_deviation) ----
  syntax Float ::= divFloatIntV(Float, Int) [function, total, symbol(divFloatIntV), no-evaluators]
  rule divFloatIntV(F:Float, I:Int) => F /Float Int2Float(I, 53, 11) [concrete]
  rule applyBin("/", F:Float, I:Int) => divFloatIntV(F, I)

  // ---- int -> float promotion for the remaining mixed arithmetic/compares ----
  syntax Float ::= intToF(Int) [function, total, symbol(intToF), no-evaluators]
  rule intToF(I:Int) => Int2Float(I, 53, 11) [concrete]
  rule applyBin("+", I:Int, F:Float) => addF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("+", F:Float, I:Int) => addF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyBin("-", I:Int, F:Float) => subF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("-", F:Float, I:Int) => subF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyBin("*", I:Int, F:Float) => mulF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("*", F:Float, I:Int) => mulF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyCmp("<", I:Int, F:Float) => floatLt(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp("<", F:Float, I:Int) => floatLt(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyCmp(">", I:Int, F:Float) => gtF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp(">", F:Float, I:Int) => gtF(F, intToF(I))

  // ---- conversions: int(float) truncates toward zero; float(int); round; math.sqrt ----
  syntax Int ::= truncF(Float) [function, total, symbol(truncF), no-evaluators]
  rule truncF(F:Float) => #if F >=Float 0.0 #then Float2Int(floorFloat(F)) #else Float2Int(ceilFloat(F)) #fi [concrete]
  rule applyBuiltin("int", F:Float, .Vals) => truncF(F)

  rule applyBuiltin("float", I:Int, .Vals)   => intToF(I)
  rule applyBuiltin("float", F:Float, .Vals) => F

  // round: Python half-even (banker's); round(F, N) scales by 10^N
  syntax Int ::= roundF(Float) [function, total, symbol(roundF), no-evaluators]
  rule roundF(F:Float)
    => #if (F -Float floorFloat(F)) ==Float 0.5
       #then (#if Float2Int(floorFloat(F)) %Int 2 ==Int 0
              #then Float2Int(floorFloat(F)) #else Float2Int(ceilFloat(F)) #fi)
       #else Float2Int(floorFloat(F +Float 0.5)) #fi [concrete]
  syntax Float ::= roundFN(Float, Int) [function, total, symbol(roundFN), no-evaluators]
  rule roundFN(F:Float, N:Int)
    => Int2Float(roundF(F *Float Int2Float(10 ^Int N, 53, 11)), 53, 11)
       /Float Int2Float(10 ^Int N, 53, 11) [concrete]
  rule applyBuiltin("round", F:Float, .Vals)        => roundF(F)
  rule applyBuiltin("round", F:Float, N:Int, .Vals) => roundFN(F, N)

  syntax Float ::= sqrtF(Float) [function, total, symbol(sqrtF), no-evaluators]
  rule sqrtF(F:Float) => sqrtFloat(F) [concrete]
  syntax KItem ::= "#mathSqrt"
  rule <k> Call(Attribute(Name("math"), "sqrt"), (E:Expr, .Exprs)) => E ~> #mathSqrt ... </k> [priority(40)]
  rule <k> F:Float ~> #mathSqrt => sqrtF(F) ... </k>
  rule <k> I:Int ~> #mathSqrt => sqrtF(intToF(I)) ... </k>

  // ---- min / max over a FLOAT list — FLOAT branch of the shared #minCont0/#maxCont0 folds (which
  // seed/step with `requires isInt(V)`, so they are STUCK on floats). These add the `requires
  // isFloat(V)` seed + a Float-accumulator fold via K's minFloat/maxFloat — concrete for krun. A proof
  // over a SYMBOLIC float list intercepts min/max problem-locally to an opaque minVF/maxVF (at
  // #applyK, priority 40, in its verification.k) BEFORE #minAcc0, so this fold is krun-only. Additive:
  // the isFloat guard is disjoint from the existing isInt one.
  syntax KItem ::= #maxAccF(Iterable, Float) | #maxContF(Float)
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxCont0 => #maxAccF(R, {V}:>Float) ... </k> requires isFloat(V)
  rule <k> #maxAccF(IT:Iterable, M:Float) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #maxContF(M) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #maxContF(M:Float) => M ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxContF(M:Float) => #maxAccF(R, maxFloat(M, {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
       requires isFloat(V)

  syntax KItem ::= #minAccF(Iterable, Float) | #minContF(Float)
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minCont0 => #minAccF(R, {V}:>Float) ... </k> requires isFloat(V)
  rule <k> #minAccF(IT:Iterable, M:Float) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #minContF(M) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #minContF(M:Float) => M ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minContF(M:Float) => #minAccF(R, minFloat(M, {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
       requires isFloat(V)

  // ---- sum over a float list (krun; mirrors the min/max float paths). The Int-only shared
  // #sumCont sticks on a Float yield; switch to a Float-headed fold via addF (concrete twin).
  // The switch guard carries the SYNTACTIC negation of the Int rule's guard so a symbolic proof
  // with isInt(V) in its path condition refutes this branch without sort reasoning.
  syntax KItem ::= #sumAccF(Iterable, Float) | #sumContF(Float)
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumCont(ACC:Int)
        => #sumAccF(R, addF(intToF(ACC), {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
       requires isFloat(V) andBool notBool (isInt(V) orBool isBool(V))
  rule <k> #sumAccF(IT:Iterable, ACC:Float) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #sumContF(ACC) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #sumContF(ACC:Float) => ACC ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumContF(ACC:Float)
        => #sumAccF(R, addF(ACC, {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
       requires isFloat(V)
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumContF(ACC:Float)
        => #sumAccF(R, addF(ACC, intToF(intOf(V)))) ... </k>
       requires isInt(V) orBool isBool(V)
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/operators.k — MPY-OPERATORS
// The operator DISPATCH layer: operands evaluate by strictness (heat/cool over KResult=Val),
// the cooled node hands to applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp (declared in core.k; each domain file
// owns its cases — bool.k, int.k, float.k, str.k, list.k, tuple.k, set.k, dict.k).

module MPY-OPERATORS
  imports MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-ITER

  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, V:Val) => applyUn(OP, V) ... </k>

  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, R:Val) => applyBin(OP, L, R) ... </k>

  // Compare's right operand sits under the CmpOp wrapper — contexts instead of attributes
  context Compare(HOLE, _)
  context Compare(_:Val, CmpOp(_, HOLE))
  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, RV:Val)) => applyCmp(OP, LV, RV) ... </k> [owise]

  rule applyCmp("is",     V:Val, noneV) => V ==K noneV
  rule applyCmp("is not", V:Val, noneV) => notBool (V ==K noneV)

  // ==== operand deref: heap objects combine/compare by STRUCTURE ============
  // (Python: list == is structural; identity only via `is`.) priority(40)
  // preempts the generic dispatch so applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp never see a ref.
  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int), R:Expr) => BinOp(OP, V, R) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, ref(H:Int)) => BinOp(OP, L, V) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       requires notBool isRefV(L)
       [priority(40)]

  // the left operand of `in`/`not in` is an ELEMENT (compares by ==K) — never deref'd
  rule <k> Compare(ref(H:Int), CmpOp(OP:String, R:Expr)) => Compare(V, CmpOp(OP, R)) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       requires OP =/=String "in" andBool OP =/=String "not in"
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> Compare(L:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int))) => Compare(L, CmpOp(OP, V)) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       requires notBool isRefV(L)
        orBool OP ==String "in" orBool OP ==String "not in"
       [priority(40)]

  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int)) => UnaryOp(OP, V) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       [priority(40)]
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/iter.k — MPY-ITER
// The iterator protocol, DECLARATION ONLY. Each iterable's #iterNext case lives in that
// iterable's own module (list/tuple/str in their modules, rangeObj in range.k, zip in
// builtins.k). Consumers (the for-loop, `x in _`, sum/all/any/max/min) import this.

module MPY-ITER
  imports MPY-CORE
  syntax KItem ::= #iterNext(Iterable) | "#iterDone" | #iterYield(Val, Iterable)
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/controls.k — MPY-CONTROLS

module MPY-CONTROLS
  imports MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-TUPLE
  imports MPY-ITER

  // ==== Assign / AugAssign (write the current scope; RHS evaluated by strictness) ==
  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => #cellW({M[X]}:>Val, V) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
        andBool X in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[X]}:>Val)
       [priority(40)]

  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- applyBin(OP, {M[X]}:>Val, V) ], _) ... </scopes>
       requires X in_keys(M)
  // `lst += [..]` where lst is a heap ref: the generic rule leaves applyBin(OP, ref, V) — but the
  // ref-deref preemption is BinOp-level (operators.k), so applyBin never derefs and it sticks. Route
  // the ref case through BinOp so the deref + list-concat + #alloc path fires (result is a fresh ref).
  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => Assign(Name(X), BinOp(OP, Name(X), V)) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
       [priority(40)]

  // ==== import trivia: `from math import floor, ceil` binds the supported
  // names as builtins in the current scope; every other import is a no-op
  rule <k> ImportFrom("math", NS:ParamNames) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
  rule <k> ImportFrom(_:String, _:ParamNames) => .K ... </k> [owise]
  syntax KItem ::= #bindImports(ParamNames)
  rule <k> #bindImports(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ N <- builtinV(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
       requires N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil"
  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
       requires notBool (N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil")

  // ==== Expr statement: evaluate for effect, discard the value ===============
  // (bare calls — mutator methods, docstrings; the WP0 statement-trivia rung)
  rule <k> Expr(_:Val) => .K ... </k>

  // ==== If (condition evaluated by strictness) ==============================
  syntax KItem ::= #branch(Bool, Stmts, Stmts)
  rule <k> If(C:Val, T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => #branch(truthy(C), T, E) ... </k>
  rule <k> #branch(true,  T:Stmts, _:Stmts) => T ... </k>
  rule <k> #branch(false, _:Stmts, E:Stmts) => E ... </k>

  // ==== IfExp: ternary T if C else E ========================================

    45	  rule deepEqV(ref(H:Int), B:Val, HP:Map) => deepEqV({HP[H]}:>Val, B, HP)
    46	       requires H in_keys(HP)
    47	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, ref(H:Int), HP:Map) => deepEqV(A, {HP[H]}:>Val, HP)
    48	       requires notBool isRefV(A) andBool H in_keys(HP)
    49	  rule deepEqV(list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq), HP:Map) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP)
    50	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, B:Val, _:Map) => A ==K B [owise]
    51	
    52	  // ==== mutator: xs.append(v) — an in-place heap write ======================
    53	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "append")), (V:Val, .Vals)) => noneV ... </k>
    54	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq))) ... </heap>
    55	       [priority(40)]
    56	
    57	  // ==== `x in list` — a <k>-cell fold over #iterNext ========================
    58	  syntax KItem ::= #memberAcc(Val, Iterable) | #memberCont(Val) | "#notB"
    59	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ... </k>
    60	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
    61	  rule <k> #memberAcc(V:Val, IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #memberCont(V) ... </k>
    62	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #memberCont(_V:Val) => false ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => true ... </k>
    64	       requires E ==K V
    65	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => #memberAcc(V, R) ... </k>
    66	       requires notBool (E ==K V)
    67	  rule <k> B:Bool ~> #notB => notBool B ... </k>
    68	endmodule

     3	module MPY-METHODS

     9	  // method-call routing + arg-eval live in call.k; this module owns applyMethod.
    10	  syntax Val ::= applyMethod(Val, String, Vals) [function]
    11	
    12	  // ==== string predicates (Python semantics) =================================
    13	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "isupper", .Vals) => hasUpper(CS) andBool notBool hasLower(CS)
    14	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "islower", .Vals) => hasLower(CS) andBool notBool hasUpper(CS)
    15	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "isalpha", .Vals) => notBool (CS ==K .IntSeq) andBool allAlpha(CS)
    16	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "isdigit", .Vals) => notBool (CS ==K .IntSeq) andBool allDigit(CS)
    17	
    18	  // ==== case maps ============================================================
    19	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "lower",    .Vals) => str(mapLower(CS))
    20	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "upper",    .Vals) => str(mapUpper(CS))
    21	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "swapcase", .Vals) => str(mapSwap(CS))
    22	
    23	  // ==== join / count / strip / encode ========================================
    24	  // S.join(list-of-str): fold with separator codes (receiver + arg deref'd by
    25	  // the call layer; the result str is a value)
    26	  rule applyMethod(str(SEP:IntSeq), "join", list(VS:ValSeq), .Vals) => str(joinCodes(SEP, VS))
    27	  syntax IntSeq ::= joinCodes(IntSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    28	  rule joinCodes(_:IntSeq, .ValSeq) => .IntSeq
    29	  rule joinCodes(_:IntSeq, vCons(str(CS:IntSeq), .ValSeq)) => CS
    30	  rule joinCodes(SEP:IntSeq, vCons(str(CS:IntSeq), vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)))
    31	    => seqConcat(CS, seqConcat(SEP, joinCodes(SEP, vCons(V, R))))
    32	
    33	  // S.count(sub): non-overlapping window scan (Python str.count)
    34	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "count", str(PC:IntSeq), .Vals) => cntSub(CS, PC)
    35	  syntax Int ::= cntSub(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function]
    36	  rule cntSub(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq) => 0
    37	  rule cntSub(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), PC:IntSeq) => 1 +Int cntSub(dropIS(iCons(C, R), isLen(PC)), PC)
    38	       requires strPrefix(PC, iCons(C, R)) andBool isLen(PC) >Int 0
    39	  rule cntSub(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), PC:IntSeq) => cntSub(R, PC)

    41	  syntax IntSeq ::= dropIS(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
    42	  rule dropIS(S:IntSeq, N:Int) => S requires N <=Int 0
    43	  rule dropIS(.IntSeq, _:Int) => .IntSeq [owise]
    44	  rule dropIS(iCons(_:Int, R:IntSeq), N:Int) => dropIS(R, N -Int 1) requires N >Int 0
    45	
    46	  // S.strip(): trim whitespace runs from both ends
    47	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "strip", .Vals) => str(revIS(trimWS(revIS(trimWS(CS)))))
    48	  syntax IntSeq ::= trimWS(IntSeq) [function, total]
    49	  rule trimWS(.IntSeq) => .IntSeq
    50	  rule trimWS(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => trimWS(R) requires isWSC(C)
    51	  rule trimWS(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => iCons(C, R) requires notBool isWSC(C)
    52	  syntax IntSeq ::= revIS(IntSeq) [function, total] | revISAcc(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    53	  rule revIS(S:IntSeq) => revISAcc(S, .IntSeq)
    54	  rule revISAcc(.IntSeq, A:IntSeq) => A
    55	  rule revISAcc(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), A:IntSeq) => revISAcc(R, iCons(C, A))
    56	
    57	  // S.encode('ascii'): identity on the code-sequence model (bytes == codes)
    58	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "encode", str(_:IntSeq), .Vals) => str(CS)
    59	
    60	  // ==== prefix ===============================================================
    61	  rule applyMethod(str(XC:IntSeq), "startswith", str(PC:IntSeq), .Vals) => startsWith(PC, XC)
    62	
    63	  // ==== list.count(v) — number of occurrences of v in the list (concrete for krun) ==========
    64	  rule applyMethod(list(VS:ValSeq), "count", V:Val, .Vals) => cntOccVS(VS, V)
    65	  syntax Int ::= cntOccVS(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    66	  rule cntOccVS(.ValSeq, _:Val)                => 0
    67	  rule cntOccVS(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), V:Val) => 1 +Int cntOccVS(R, V) requires A ==K V
    68	  rule cntOccVS(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), V:Val) => cntOccVS(R, V)        requires notBool (A ==K V)
    69	
    70	  // ==== split (no-arg: on whitespace runs, dropping empty tokens) + replace (single char) ==========
    71	  // Concrete string ops for krun. A proof over a symbolic string intercepts the split problem-locally.
    72	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(str(CS:IntSeq), "split")), .Vals)
    73	        => #alloc(list(splitWS(CS, .IntSeq, .ValSeq))) ... </k>
    74	       [priority(40)]
    75	  syntax ValSeq ::= splitWS(IntSeq, IntSeq, ValSeq) [function]  // remaining, current token, result
    76	  rule splitWS(.IntSeq, CUR:IntSeq, ACC:ValSeq) => flushTok(ACC, CUR)
    77	  rule splitWS(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), CUR:IntSeq, ACC:ValSeq) => splitWS(R, .IntSeq, flushTok(ACC, CUR))
    78	       requires isWSC(C)
    79	  rule splitWS(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), CUR:IntSeq, ACC:ValSeq) => splitWS(R, seqConcat(CUR, iCons(C, .IntSeq)), ACC)
    80	       requires notBool isWSC(C)
    81	  // flush the current token to the result list iff non-empty.
    82	  syntax ValSeq ::= flushTok(ValSeq, IntSeq) [function]
    83	  rule flushTok(ACC:ValSeq, .IntSeq)            => ACC
    84	  rule flushTok(ACC:ValSeq, iCons(C:Int, T:IntSeq)) => valSeqConcat(ACC, vCons(str(iCons(C, T)), .ValSeq))
    85	  syntax Bool ::= isWSC(Int) [function, total]
    86	  rule isWSC(C:Int) => C ==Int 32 orBool C ==Int 9 orBool C ==Int 10 orBool C ==Int 13
    87	
    88	  // split(sep='x') keyword form delegates to the positional k-cell rule
    89	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(str(CS:IntSeq), "split")), (kwV("sep", str(S:IntSeq)), .Vals))
    90	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(str(CS), "split")), (str(S), .Vals)) ... </k>
    91	       [priority(39)]
    92	
    93	  // str.split(sep) — single-char separator, KEEPING empty parts (Python's sep-split; len == #sep + 1).
    94	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(str(CS:IntSeq), "split")), (str(iCons(SEP:Int, .IntSeq)), .Vals))
    95	        => #alloc(list(splitSep(CS, SEP, .IntSeq))) ... </k>
    96	       [priority(40)]
    97	  syntax ValSeq ::= splitSep(IntSeq, Int, IntSeq) [function]  // remaining, sep code, current token
    98	  rule splitSep(.IntSeq, _SEP:Int, CUR:IntSeq)              => vCons(str(CUR), .ValSeq)
    99	  rule splitSep(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), SEP:Int, CUR:IntSeq) => vCons(str(CUR), splitSep(R, SEP, .IntSeq))
   100	       requires C ==Int SEP
   101	  rule splitSep(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), SEP:Int, CUR:IntSeq) => splitSep(R, SEP, seqConcat(CUR, iCons(C, .IntSeq)))
   102	       requires notBool (C ==Int SEP)
   103	
   104	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "replace", str(iCons(A:Int, .IntSeq)), str(iCons(B:Int, .IntSeq)), .Vals)
   105	    => str(replaceC(CS, A, B))
   106	  syntax IntSeq ::= replaceC(IntSeq, Int, Int) [function, total]
   107	  rule replaceC(.IntSeq, _:Int, _:Int)             => .IntSeq
   108	  rule replaceC(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), A:Int, B:Int) => iCons(B, replaceC(R, A, B)) requires C ==Int A
   109	  rule replaceC(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), A:Int, B:Int) => iCons(C, replaceC(R, A, B)) requires notBool (C ==Int A)
   110	
   111	  // ==== char helpers =========================================================
   112	  syntax Bool ::= isUpperC(Int) [function, total]
   113	  rule isUpperC(C:Int) => C >=Int 65 andBool C <=Int 90
   114	
   115	  syntax Bool ::= isLowerC(Int) [function, total]
   116	  rule isLowerC(C:Int) => C >=Int 97 andBool C <=Int 122
   117	
   118	  syntax Bool ::= isAlphaC(Int) [function, total]
   119	  rule isAlphaC(C:Int) => isUpperC(C) orBool isLowerC(C)
   120	
   121	  syntax Bool ::= isDigitC(Int) [function, total]
   122	  rule isDigitC(C:Int) => C >=Int 48 andBool C <=Int 57
   123	
   124	  syntax Bool ::= hasUpper(IntSeq) [function, total]
   125	  rule hasUpper(.IntSeq) => false
   126	  rule hasUpper(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => isUpperC(C) orBool hasUpper(S)
   127	
   128	  syntax Bool ::= hasLower(IntSeq) [function, total]
   129	  rule hasLower(.IntSeq) => false
   130	  rule hasLower(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => isLowerC(C) orBool hasLower(S)
   131	
   132	  syntax Bool ::= allAlpha(IntSeq) [function, total]
   133	  rule allAlpha(.IntSeq) => true
   134	  rule allAlpha(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => isAlphaC(C) andBool allAlpha(S)
   135	
   136	  syntax Bool ::= allDigit(IntSeq) [function, total]
   137	  rule allDigit(.IntSeq) => true
   138	  rule allDigit(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => isDigitC(C) andBool allDigit(S)
   139	
   140	  syntax Int ::= lowerC(Int) [function, total]
   141	
   142	  rule lowerC(C:Int) => C +Int 32 requires isUpperC(C)
   143	  rule lowerC(C:Int) => C         [owise]
   144	
   145	  syntax Int ::= upperC(Int) [function, total]
   146	  rule upperC(C:Int) => C -Int 32 requires isLowerC(C)
   147	  rule upperC(C:Int) => C         [owise]
   148	
   149	  syntax Int ::= swapC(Int) [function, total]
   150	  rule swapC(C:Int) => C +Int 32 requires isUpperC(C)
   151	  rule swapC(C:Int) => C -Int 32 requires isLowerC(C)
   152	  rule swapC(C:Int) => C         [owise]
   153	
   154	  syntax IntSeq ::= mapLower(IntSeq) [function, total]
   155	  rule mapLower(.IntSeq) => .IntSeq
   156	  rule mapLower(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => iCons(lowerC(C), mapLower(S))
   157	
   158	  syntax IntSeq ::= mapUpper(IntSeq) [function, total]
   159	  rule mapUpper(.IntSeq) => .IntSeq
   160	  rule mapUpper(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => iCons(upperC(C), mapUpper(S))
   161	
   162	  syntax IntSeq ::= mapSwap(IntSeq) [function, total]

   164	  rule mapSwap(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => iCons(swapC(C), mapSwap(S))

   166	  syntax Bool ::= startsWith(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]

   168	  rule startsWith(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false

     3	module MPY-FUNCTIONS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // call routing + callee/arg evaluation (#callee/#args/#argCont) live in call.k;
     7	  // this module owns the frame lifecycle (bind params, return, pop).
     8	  syntax KItem ::= frame(continuation: K, callerEnv: Int, savedLoc: Int)
     9	                 | #bindP(ParamNames, Vals)
    10	                 | "#pop"
    11	                 | "#endcall"
    12	
    13	  // ==== def / anonymous closure =============================================
    14	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    15	       <env> L:Int </env>
    16	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ], _) ... </scopes>
    17	
    18	  syntax Expr ::= closureExpr(ParamNames, Stmts)
    19	  rule <k> closureExpr(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts) => closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ... </k>
    20	       <env> L:Int </env>
    21	
    22	  // ==== annotated def/lambda (closure cells; spec 2.3) ======================
    23	  // closureValC(params, cellvars, body, captured-cells). No frame anchor: all
    24	  // enclosing-local reads are freevars (symtable-complete) and go through the
    25	  // captured cells; everything else is global/builtin, so the callee frame's
    26	  // parent is the module scope (0) — sound after the defining frame dies.
    27	  syntax Val ::= closureValC(ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    28	
    29	  // capture: resolve each freevar to the enclosing frame's cellRef, then bind
    30	  // (FuncDef) or yield (Lambda) the closure value.
    31	  syntax KItem ::= #mkClosure(String, ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    32	                 | #mkLambda(ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    33	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    34	                   FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts)
    35	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVS, BODY, .Map) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    37	                      (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    38	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    39	       <env> L:Int </env>
    40	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    41	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    42	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    43	                      .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map) => .K ... </k>
    44	       <env> L:Int </env>
    45	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ], _) ... </scopes>
    46	
    47	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    48	        => closureVal(PNS, Return(E) .Stmts, L) ... </k>
    49	       <env> L:Int </env>
    50	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    51	                  FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    52	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVS, Return(E) .Stmts, .Map) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    54	                     (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    55	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    56	       <env> L:Int </env>
    57	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    58	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    59	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    60	        => closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ... </k>
    61	
    62	  // ==== bind params ========================================================
    63	  rule <k> #bindP(.ParamNames, .Vals) => .K ... </k>
    64	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals)) => #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    65	       <env> L:Int </env>
    66	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ P <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
    67	  // a param that is a cellvar was pre-bound to its cell at frame entry
    68	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals))
    69	        => #cellW({M[P]}:>Val, V) ~> #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    70	       <env> L:Int </env>
    71	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    72	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    73	        andBool pnMember(P, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
    74	        andBool P in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[P]}:>Val)
    75	       [priority(40)]
    76	
    77	  // ==== return / pop the frame (the returned expr evaluates by strictness) ==
    78	  rule <k> Return(V:Val) ~> _ => #pop </k>
    79	       <ret> noRet => retV(V) </ret>
    80	  rule <k> #endcall => #pop ... </k>
    81	       <ret> noRet => retV(noneV) </ret>
    82	  // pop: restore env, DEALLOCATE the callee frame, and wind scopeLoc back (LIFO allocation
    83	  // makes the saved loc the callee frame's own loc). Sound because no closureVal outlives its
    84	  // defining frame (frontend subset: no returned/stored closures; module defs live in loc 0).
    85	  rule <k> #pop => V ~> CONT </k>
    86	       <ret>   retV(V) => noRet </ret>
    87	       <stack> ListItem(frame(CONT:K, CALLERL:Int, SAVEDL:Int)) => .List ... </stack>
    88	       <env>   L:Int => CALLERL </env>
    89	       <scopes> SC:Map => SC [ L <- undef ] </scopes>
    90	       <scopeLoc> _ => SAVEDL </scopeLoc>
    91	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/call.k — MPY-CALL
     2	// ONE call route for every callable: evaluate the callee to a VALUE (name lookup reaches
     3	// builtins at the root; a cooled Attribute is a bound method), evaluate the args (the shared
     4	// #evalArgs loop in core.k), then dispatch on the callee value:
     5	//   closureVal    -> bind params, push a frame (user function)
     6	//   boundMethodV  -> applyMethod
     7	//   builtinV      -> the #iterNext folds (sum/all/any/max/min) or applyBuiltin
     8	//   typeV         -> callable type objects: int(...) / str(...)
     9	
    10	module MPY-CALL
    11	  imports MPY-METHODS
    12	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    13	  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS
    14	
    15	  // a cooled attribute is a bound method value
    16	  rule <k> Attribute(V:Val, M:String) => boundMethodV(V, M) ... </k>
    17	
    18	  // evaluate callee, then args ([owise]: problem-local Call interceptions beat this)
    19	  syntax KItem ::= #callee(Exprs)
    20	  rule <k> Call(Fe:Expr, ARGS:Exprs) => Fe ~> #callee(ARGS) ... </k> [owise]
    21	  rule <k> CV:Val ~> #callee(ARGS:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ARGS, .Vals, toCall(CV)) ... </k>
    22	
    23	  // ==== dispatch on the callee value ========================================
    24	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyMethod(OBJ, M, ACC) ... </k>
    25	
    26	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sum")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #sumAcc(OBJ, 0) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("all")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #allAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("any")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #anyAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    29	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("max")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #maxAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("min")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #minAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    31	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(BN, ACC) ... </k> [owise]
    32	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)),     ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(T, ACC)  ... </k>
    33	
    34	  // ==== heap-object arguments/receivers =====================================
    35	  // Builtins and type calls READ structure — deref the first two arg positions
    36	  // (covers len/sum/all/any/max/min/sorted/list/set + zip's pair). Mutating list
    37	  // methods take the ref itself; every other method receiver is deref'd.
    38	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    39	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    40	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    41	       [priority(40)]
    42	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (A:Val, ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    43	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (A, V, REST)) ... </k>
    44	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    45	       requires notBool isRefV(A)
    46	       [priority(40)]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exhaustive source-level inventory of K declarations and rules in audit scope."""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import re
from pathlib import Path


REFERENCE_ROOT = Path("/reference/reference-semantics")
EXTRA_FILES = [Path("/candidate/verification.k"), Path("/candidate/spec.k")]
OUTPUT = Path("/audit-output/evidence/rule-inventory.txt")

START = re.compile(
    r"^(?:requires\b|module\b|endmodule\b|"
    r"  (?:imports\b|syntax\b|configuration\b|context\b|rule\b|claim\b))"
)


def kind_of(text: str) -> str:
    stripped = text.lstrip()
    for kind in (
        "requires",
        "module",
        "endmodule",
        "imports",
        "syntax",
        "configuration",
        "context",
        "rule",
        "claim",
    ):
        if stripped.startswith(kind):
            return kind
    return "unknown"


def blocks(path: Path):
    lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    starts = [index for index, line in enumerate(lines) if START.match(line)]
    for position, start in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[position + 1] if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
        chunk = lines[start:end]
        while chunk and (not chunk[-1].strip() or chunk[-1].lstrip().startswith("//")):
            chunk.pop()
        if not chunk:
            continue
        text = "\n".join(chunk)
        yield start + 1, kind_of(text), text


def normalize(text: str) -> str:
    content = []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        code = line.split("//", 1)[0].strip()
        if code:
            content.append(code)
    return " ".join(content)


def attributes(text: str) -> str:
    names = []
    for attribute_group in re.findall(r"\[([^\]]+)\]", text):
        for item in attribute_group.split(","):
            name = item.strip()
            if name:
                names.append(name)
    if "no-evaluators" in text and "no-evaluators" not in names:
        names.append("no-evaluators")
    return ",".join(names) if names else "-"


def main() -> int:
    files = sorted(REFERENCE_ROOT.rglob("*.k")) + EXTRA_FILES
    counts = collections.Counter()
    file_counts: dict[str, collections.Counter] = {}
    entries = []

    for path in files:
        relative = (
            "reference-semantics/" + path.relative_to(REFERENCE_ROOT).as_posix()
            if path.is_relative_to(REFERENCE_ROOT)
            else "candidate/" + path.name
        )
        local = collections.Counter()
        for line, kind, text in blocks(path):
            counts[kind] += 1
            local[kind] += 1
            entries.append((relative, line, kind, attributes(text), normalize(text)))
        file_counts[relative] = local

    output = []
    output.append("K SOURCE INVENTORY")
    output.append("==================")
    output.append(f"files={len(files)}")
    output.append("total_counts=" + " ".join(f"{key}:{counts[key]}" for key in sorted(counts)))
    output.append("")
    output.append("PER-FILE COUNTS")
    output.append("----------------")
    for relative in sorted(file_counts):
        local = file_counts[relative]
        output.append(
            relative + " " + " ".join(f"{key}:{local[key]}" for key in sorted(local))
        )
    output.append("")
    output.append("EVERY DECLARATION / RULE / CLAIM")
    output.append("--------------------------------")
    for relative, line, kind, attrs, text in entries:
        output.append(f"{relative}:{line}\t{kind}\tattrs={attrs}\t{text}")
    output.append("")

    OUTPUT.write_text("\n".join(output), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"inventory={OUTPUT}")
    print(f"files={len(files)}")
    print("total_counts=" + " ".join(f"{key}:{counts[key]}" for key in sorted(counts)))
    for relative in sorted(file_counts):
        local = file_counts[relative]
        print(relative + " " + " ".join(f"{key}:{local[key]}" for key in sorted(local)))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Decode the observed result heaps in the fresh LLVM krun log."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path


LOG = Path("/audit-output/evidence/concrete-run.log")


def heap_entry_line(text: str, address: int) -> str:
    pattern = re.compile(rf"^    {address} \|-> list \(.*$", re.MULTILINE)
    match = pattern.search(text)
    if match is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"heap entry {address} not found")
    return match.group(0)


def balanced_segment(text: str, open_paren: int) -> str:
    depth = 0
    for index in range(open_paren, len(text)):
        if text[index] == "(":
            depth += 1
        elif text[index] == ")":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return text[open_paren : index + 1]
    raise AssertionError("unbalanced K term")


def decode_strings(line: str) -> list[str]:
    decoded = []
    cursor = 0
    while True:
        start = line.find("str (", cursor)
        if start < 0:
            return decoded
        open_paren = line.find("(", start)
        segment = balanced_segment(line, open_paren)
        codes = [int(code) for code in re.findall(r"iCons \( (-?\d+) ,", segment)]
        decoded.append("".join(chr(code) for code in codes))
        cursor = open_paren + len(segment)


def main() -> int:
    text = LOG.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert "<k>\n    .K\n  </k>" in text
    assert "<exc>\n    NoExc\n  </exc>" in text
    assert "<exit-code>\n    0\n  </exit-code>" in text
    assert '"observed_example" |-> ref ( 1 )' in text
    assert '"observed_boundaries" |-> ref ( 3 )' in text
    assert '"observed_empty" |-> ref ( 5 )' in text

    expected_example = ["A+", "B", "C-", "C", "A-"]
    expected_boundaries = [
        "A+", "A", "A-", "A-", "B+", "B+", "B", "B", "B-",
        "B-", "C+", "C+", "C", "C", "C-", "C-", "D+", "D+",
        "D", "D", "D-", "D-", "E", "E", "A",
    ]
    actual_example = decode_strings(heap_entry_line(text, 1))
    actual_boundaries = decode_strings(heap_entry_line(text, 3))
    empty_line = heap_entry_line(text, 5)

    assert actual_example == expected_example, (actual_example, expected_example)
    assert actual_boundaries == expected_boundaries, (
        actual_boundaries,
        expected_boundaries,
    )
    assert "list ( .ValSeq )" in empty_line
    print(f"example={actual_example}")
    print(f"boundaries={actual_boundaries}")
    print("empty=[]")
    print("concrete_output_match=True")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

+def numerical_letter_grade(grades):
+    letter_grades = []
+    for grade in grades:
+        if grade == 4.0:
+            letter_grades.append("A+")
+        elif grade > 3.7:
+            letter_grades.append("A")
+        elif grade > 3.3:
+            letter_grades.append("A-")
+        elif grade > 3.0:
+            letter_grades.append("B+")
+        elif grade > 2.7:
+            letter_grades.append("B")
+        elif grade > 2.3:
+            letter_grades.append("B-")
+        elif grade > 2.0:
+            letter_grades.append("C+")
+        elif grade > 1.7:
+            letter_grades.append("C")
+        elif grade > 1.3:
+            letter_grades.append("C-")
+        elif grade > 1.0:
+            letter_grades.append("D+")
+        elif grade > 0.7:
+            letter_grades.append("D")
+        elif grade > 0.0:
+            letter_grades.append("D-")
+        else:
+            letter_grades.append("E")
+    return letter_grades

# What is proven

Under the supplied MPY semantics, `numerical_letter_grade` is partially
correct for every arbitrary finite list whose elements are MPY `Int` or
`Float` values. There is no bound on list length and no finite unrolling in
the target theorem.

For an input sequence `VS`, the function returns a fresh list containing one
letter-grade string per input, in the same order. Each output is selected by
the table encoded by `gradeValue`: equality with `4.0` gives `A+`; otherwise
the strict descending cutoffs give `A` through `D-`; otherwise the result is
`E`.

The proof executes the translated function body, including module loading,
name lookup, call-frame creation, parameter binding, list allocation, every
comparison and branch, `append`, return lookup, frame pop, and restoration of
the caller state. It does not replace the function or loop with an
operational summary.

This is a reachability/partial-correctness result. It is not a separate
machine-checked liveness theorem.

<heap> .Map => 0 |-> list(gradeAcc(.ValSeq, VS)) </heap>
<heapLoc> 0 => 1 </heapLoc>
<env> 0 => 0 </env>
